purpose: Independent blind second read of a deterministic stratified sample of Map IV counties, to be adjudicated against the full trace in lib/map4-county-trace.json. That file was not opened at any point during this read, and no commit or log entry about it was read.

sampling_rule.universe: lib/counties-conus-fips.json, 3,108 CONUS plus DC county equivalents
sampling_rule.rule: Sort all 3,108 canonical FIPS ascending as zero-padded strings. Take every 7th starting at index 0, that is indices 0, 7, 14, ... 3101.
sampling_rule.deviation_note: The brief asked for 400 counties drawn by taking every 7th and then topping up to 400 from the remainder at the same stride offset. Stride 7 over 3,108 yields 444, not fewer than 400, so the top-up step is moot. Truncating the stride sequence at 400 would have stopped at FIPS 48xxx and dropped Utah, Vermont, Virginia, Washington, West Virginia, Wisconsin and Wyoming entirely, which is a worse sample. The full 444 are read and reported. The draw is reproducible from the rule above and was fixed before any county was looked at.
sampling_rule.known_gaps: Stride 7 happens to select no county in DC (1 county) or Rhode Island (5 counties). No county was hand added or hand removed.

method.identification: Modern county mesh projected onto plate pixels with the shipped order-3 georef. Per county the largest ring is rasterised, eroded by 4 px, and the largest inscribed square inside the eroded mask is taken as the measurement window.
method.reading: Every county was looked at as an 8x crop with the measurement window marked by corner ticks, 20 counties to a contact sheet, 23 sheets. Regional views at 3x to 6x were used where a patch boundary or a numeral needed context. Structure and stroke weight decided the verdict; the measurements below were a numeric aid, never the verdict.
method.measurements: lib/plate_measure.py Radon path for orientation and perpendicular period, plus stroke width. Two extra discriminators were built for this read and are described in findings.
method.numerals: A numeral is appended only where a circle was actually legible in the county or in the same contiguous same-texture patch in a regional view. No numeral was inferred from geography alone.

confidence_vocabulary.firm: structure and, where relevant, the numeral were read unambiguously in the county itself
confidence_vocabulary.leaning: the mark is the best fit but the window is small, straddles a patch edge, or the family rank is close
confidence_vocabulary.unreadable: no usable window: label box, coast or river ink, independent city, or mesh offset larger than the county

findings_on_the_legend.claim: plate_legend_map4.VERIFIED_NUMERALS row (4246, 2384, 3, 'm4:p01', 'National Power & Light Co', 'Carolina Piedmont') is wrong.
findings_on_the_legend.evidence: At 4246,2384 and at 4232,2392 the plate shows one and the same circled 2 sitting on m4:p04 vertical rails. The two coordinates are 14 px apart and a circle is 22 to 24 px across, so they cannot be two circles. Both fall inside 45075 Orangeburg SC, which is coastal plain, not Piedmont. Two of the nine verified rows point at the same ink.
findings_on_the_legend.consequence: The scoping rule loses one of its nine supports, and m4:p01:n3 has no correct coordinate in the file.
findings_on_the_legend.repair: A genuine circled 3 on p01 mottle does exist. I read one at 47113 Madison TN, which is Tennessee Electric Power, a National Power & Light company. The reading is right; only the coordinate is wrong.

findings_on_the_legend.claim: map4-legend-patterns.md describes p13 empire-power as 'vertical rules, thinner than p09' while the same table gives both p09 and p13 stroke 4.2.
findings_on_the_legend.evidence: My own measurement of both swatches reproduces stroke 4.2 for each. They differ in period, 9.2 against 12.0, and in ink, not in weight.
findings_on_the_legend.consequence: A tracer told to break p09 from p13 on line weight will fail. The only separator is duty cycle, which is what the confusable section already says.

findings_on_the_legend.claim: The legend records ebasco as ink 0.98 in the swatch and 0.84 in the fill, with no range.
findings_on_the_legend.evidence: p01 fills measure window ink 0.30 to 0.37 across Montana, 0.35 to 0.51 across Arkansas, and 0.78 at the Louisiana delta. Montana is one continuous p01 patch carrying a circled 2, unmistakable at 4x regional zoom and easy to mistake for grey stipple or foxed paper at 8x county zoom.
findings_on_the_legend.consequence: Any ink threshold tuned to 0.84 will drop the entire northern Rockies p01 field and call it unserved or unresolved. This is the single largest systematic error available on this plate.
findings_on_the_legend.repair: Record p01 field ink as 0.30 to 0.85 and say that p01 is identified by structureless mottle with white pinhole speckle, not by darkness.

findings_on_the_legend.claim: Several fill_site place names do not match the county the coordinate lands in under the shipped georef.
findings_on_the_legend.evidence: age 'north-east Pennsylvania' 4336,1276 lands in 36123 Yates NY. new-england-power 'central Massachusetts' 4752,1180 lands in 33011 Hillsborough NH. ebasco 'Louisiana and Mississippi delta' 3270,2470 lands in 05041 Desha AR. nevada-california 'Owens Valley, eastern California' 1030,1960 lands in 32023 Nye NV. rockland 'Orange and Rockland counties' 4565,1362 lands in 36105 Sullivan NY. numeral 8 'SW Michigan' 3660,1498 lands in 18039 Elkhart IN.
findings_on_the_legend.consequence: The legend tells a tracer to break p06 from p21 'by geography'. An unreliable geography annotation makes that instruction unsafe. The textures at those coordinates are right; the place names are not.

findings_on_the_legend.claim: The legend calls p04 against p23 structural and says it is not separable in a small county. Two cheap measurements do separate them.
findings_on_the_legend.evidence: Alternation, the ratio of weak to strong peak heights in the perpendicular profile, measures 0.30 for p04 and 0.84 for p23, and 0.34 for p07 against 0.94 for p22. Dash ratio, the along-line standard deviation over the across-line standard deviation, measures 0.15 for p04 against 0.41 for p23, and separates every dashed mark (p05 0.23, p14 0.23, p20 0.44, p23 0.41) from every continuous rule (p06 0.10, p08 0.08, p09 0.04, p11 0.09, p13 0.07, p15 0.08, p16 0.13, p17 0.09, p21 0.07, p22 0.07).
findings_on_the_legend.caveat: Both hold cleanly on the 40 px swatches. In a 48 px county window the alternation test degrades: the p07 site at 54077 Preston WV returns 0.94, not the 0.34 its swatch gives. Use them as swatch-space discriminators and as a county-space hint, not a county-space rule.

findings_on_the_legend.claim: Two numerals read cleanly on a confidently identified host texture and then resolve to a company that cannot have operated there.
findings_on_the_legend.evidence: A circled 6 sits on m4:p04 rails in a small heavily outlined patch in eastern Colorado around 08073 Lincoln, and again on p04 rails in central Arizona near 1372,2258. m4:p04:n6 is United Gas Improvement, a Philadelphia company. A circled 4 sits on the m4:p02 grid at 20141 Osborne KS and 20057 Ford KS. m4:p02:n4 is Commonwealth Light & Power, which the legend itself places in northern Michigan, and I confirmed a circled 4 on the grid there at 26127 Oceana MI.
findings_on_the_legend.checks_done: I read the plate's own legend text for all three numbered lists at 4x. plate_legend_map4.NUMBERED is a verbatim correct transcription, so the list is not the problem. The host textures were identified before the numerals, per the legend's own rule.
findings_on_the_legend.consequence: Either the numeral scoping rule has an exception the legend does not state, or the FTC reused numerals across disjoint regions of one parent. Either way a trace that resolves numerals to company names without a plausibility check will publish wrong attributions. Recorded as read, not silently corrected.

findings_on_the_legend.claim: Three reading hazards not in the legend's HAZARDS list.
findings_on_the_legend.evidence: A bright washed vertical band near x 2130 behaves like the two listed folds. Rectangular western county boundaries are continuous vertical lines and mimic p04 rails when they cross p23 dash columns, which is the exact discriminator the legend relies on. Everglades swamp symbols in 12021 Collier and 12051 Hendry read as ink 0.42 to 0.75 with no fill present at all.

confirmations: p12 duke plus marks at 37027 Caldwell NC are exactly as described and are the most distinctive mark on the plate.
p18 pacific-gas-electric dot-in-diamond is unmistakable and never confusable.

The mirror-pair weight rule works. 29099 Jefferson MO reads thin wide slash and sits in Union Electric territory, which is The North American Company; 55133 Waukesha WI reads the same and sits in Milwaukee, also North American.

The numeral scoping rule survives every check it passed. Circled 2 on p04 across Alabama, Georgia, Michigan, Mississippi and South Carolina is Commonwealth & Southern in all five. Circled 11 on the p02 grid is identical in Virginia and in south Georgia, and National Electric Power owned both Virginia Public Service and Georgia Power & Light. Circled 2 on p01 covers Montana, Arizona and eastern Washington, all American Power & Light.
The legend's swatch table is sound. My independent Radon measurement of all 24 swatches reproduces its period, orientation and stroke columns.
